sections.title: THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS LOWER MO VALLEY
sections.text: ...SUMMARY... A swath of large hail, a couple tornadoes, and severe wind gusts are most likely across parts of central to northeast Montana between 4 PM and Midnight MDT. Scattered damaging winds are also possible this afternoon across the Lower Missouri Valley.

sections.title: MT to the Dakotas
sections.text: A persistent convective cluster is ongoing near the ND/SD border. This activity appears to be rooted between 800-700 mb. As modest warm theta-e advection diminishes in this layer amid rising mid-level heights, these storms should further weaken during the next couple hours. Attention turns to probable redevelopment of convection across portions of central MT during the late afternoon/early evening. Here, a corridor of stronger diabatic heating is underway between a pervasive cirrus canopy across western MT and a stratus plume over southeast MT. The combination of weak low-level easterlies contributing to upslope flow along with weak large-scale ascent through mid-level vorticity lobes ejecting within the broader trough over the Northwest should contribute to a few discrete storms developing in the Lewistown vicinity. Very strong speed shear from 700 mb up (effective values around 60 kt) will yield elongated hodographs favorable for splitting supercells. Increasing buoyancy to the east being advected by strengthening low-level southeasterlies should result in intensifying supercells during the early to mid evening as convection spreads towards northeast MT. sections.title: Lower MO Valley to southern Lower MI
sections.text: Multiple remnant convective clusters are ongoing, one centered on southeast IA and the other in the Milwaukee to Chicagoland vicinity. A pronounced outflow boundary has surged out of these clusters and does not appeared to be well handled by morning guidance. The more concerning cluster for increasing severe potential is the one in IA given a very unstable air mass developing to its south amid mid 70s surface dew points. While flow is weak, substantial veering of the wind profile with low-level southerlies to high-level north-northwesterlies could support 25-30 kt effective shear. If development can continue along the outflow boundary this afternoon, a south-southwest propagating cluster towards the Lower MO Valley is possible with damaging winds as the primary hazard.

sections.title: Lower MS Valley/Ark-La-Tex
sections.text: A convectively enhanced circulation over northwest MS should drift southwestward towards the Ark-La-Tex through the period. Ongoing convection will likely persist, increasing in intensity around peak heating as destabilization intensifies to the southwest. While deep-layer shear is weak, loosely organized multicell clustering might occur with damaging winds as the primary threat. ..Grams/Mosier.. 06/28/2019

outlooks.summary: A swath of large hail, a couple tornadoes, and severe wind gusts are most likely across parts of central to northeast Montana between 4 PM and Midnight MDT. A few damaging wind gusts and hail also remain possible this afternoon across a portion of northern Missouri into central Illinois.

sections.title: Discussion
sections.text: Primary change to previous outlook has been to adjust SLGT and MRGL risk lines over the middle MS Valley region based on current convective and mesoscale trends. Storms forming along an outflow boundary and in association with an MCV will continue to pose a risk for a few damaging wind gusts over a portion of northern MO into central IL. Otherwise outlook appears on track with primary severe threat expected to evolve across central through northern MT later this afternoon or evening as supercells develop over the higher terrain and within frontal zone and spread northeast, posing a risk for large hail, damaging wind and a couple of tornadoes. ..Dial.. 06/28/2019 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1134 AM CDT Fri Jun 28 2019/

outlooks.summary: Scattered large hail, a couple tornadoes, and severe wind gusts remain likely across parts of central to northeast Montana through about 1 AM MDT. A few damaging wind gusts and hail also remain possible this evening across a portion of the Missouri Valley and Great Lakes.

sections.title: MT into ND
sections.text: Within a strongly sheared environment, a couple of supercells capable of producing large hail, damaging winds, and a couple tornadoes remain possible across north-central into northeastern MT this evening. Instability increases with eastward extent into northeastern MT with persistent south-southeasterly low-level flow occurring across this region. Current expectations are for ongoing storms to strengthen this evening as they encounter this more unstable airmass, and scattered large hail may occur. Some of this hail could be greater than 2 inches in diameter given the strong instability and shear present. Eventually, some clustering of storms may occur as they approach western ND late tonight, with perhaps a gradual increase in the damaging wind potential. See Mesoscale Discussion 1291 for more information on the short-term severe threat across this region.

sections.title: Mid MO Valley into the Lower Great Lakes
sections.text: In the wake of an earlier MCS, it remains unclear if any additional convection will occur across parts of IA into MO this evening and overnight. A weak disturbance, likely related to northern Plains convection from yesterday, is moving southeastward across MN this evening. Some recent attempts at convection have occurred over southeastern IA along a weak front, and in central MO along an instability gradient/outflow boundary. Will maintain low-end hail/wind probabilities for a portion of this region in the event that storms do redevelop this evening or overnight. Farther east, an isolated hail/wind threat may persist in the short term across parts of northern IN into southern Lower MI along a weak front. A positively tilted shortwave trough will continue to move eastward across this region, and modest shear should support occasional updraft organization. Instability will further lessen across this region later this evening, and the marginal severe threat will likewise diminish.

sections.title: Elsewhere
sections.text: Strong to locally severe thunderstorms will continue to be possible early this evening across parts of the Southeast, Mid Atlantic, and Ohio Valley. Very isolated instances of hail and damaging winds could occur over the next hour or two. Generally weak shear and diminishing instability with the loss of daytime heating will greatly limit the potential for organized severe weather across these regions. ..Gleason.. 06/29/2019

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Strong thunderstorms should spread south into northern Missouri over the next few hours. Locally damaging winds and large hail are the expected threats.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Long-lived cluster of convection that developed over southern MN/WI region last night continues to spread south with some southwest propagation along the western flank. Well-defined outflow is racing ahead of this feature (10-20mi) at roughly 27kt, indicative of established cold pool. Strong boundary-layer heating is observed ahead of the complex into northern MO and low-level lapse rates are steepening. As CINH weakens, further propagation along the instability axis is expected. Additionally, northerly flow aloft, along the back side of a weak low noted over northern MS, will contribute to this activity spreading across northern MO.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Strong thunderstorms will spread south and east across ww457 over the next few hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Long-lived convection continues to shift south and east across northern MO/western IL at roughly 20-25kt. MCV has evolved over Henderson County IL within an expanding precip shield and this may be aiding downstream development over central IL just east of the watch. In the absence of deep thermals ahead of the MCS over central MO, strongest updrafts over the next few hours may actually focus ahead of the MCV over central IL. Even so, unless current activity strengthens a new ww is not currently anticipated. ..Darrow.. 06/28/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe thunderstorms are expected to develop within the next 1-2 hours. All severe hazards are possible with initial development with upscale growth into a linear MCS possible thereafter.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Low-level moisture continues to advect westward across central MT. Observations at LVM and BIL recently reported dewpoint increases of 4-5 degrees, with the most recent values of 54 and 58, respectively. Modified RAP sounding show very little or no remaining convective inhibition and the expectation is for convective initiation to occur within the next hour or two. Instability is expected to remain modest over much of central MT with the stronger instability across eastern MT where the dewpoints are higher. Even so, strong southwesterly flow aloft results in long hodographs supportive of an initially discrete supercell storm mode. All hazards are possible within this initial supercell mode, include a tornado or two and very large (i.e. greater than 2" in diameter) hail. After this initially discrete mode, linear growth into a well-organized MCS is possible, although its extent and severity still remain uncertain.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Pulse, airmass thunderstorms are developing across portions of the Mid-Atlantic this evening. A strong wind gust or two is possible, but a watch issuance is unlikely.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Pulse, airmass thunderstorms are developing across the Mid-Atlantic as insolation has allowed certain areas reach their convective temperatures this afternoon/evening. A warm, moist airmass is in place with surface temperatures in the upper 80s/low 90s F and dewpoints in mid 60s/low 70s F resulting in MLCAPE of 1000-2000 J/kg. With light flow/shear and modest lapse rates aloft, organized severe storms are unlikely, but isolated strong wind gusts are possible with relatively steep low-level lapse rates, especially as storms collapse. A watch issuance is unlikely given the marginal, isolated severe threat.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated storm development, perhaps with supercell structure, may pose a risk for severe hail and wind across parts of the Nebraska Sand Hills vicinity into the Badlands of South Dakota between now and 7-9 PM MDT.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: At least attempts at sustained thunderstorm development are ongoing east and southeast of Chadron NE, where low-level convergence may be locally enhanced within weak surface troughing, and convective temperatures may have been reached. This may be aided by large-scale ascent associated with a weak perturbation migrating around the northeastern periphery of elongated mid-level ridging extending northeast of the southern Rockies. However, this is occurring in the presence of considerable inhibition associated with very warm elevated mixed-layer air. The strong inhibition may limit potential for substantive upscale convective growth and, ultimately the sustenance of ongoing convective development. However, in the presence of generally weak, but modestly sheared, southwesterly deep-layer ambient mean flow, inflow of boundary layer air characterized by moderate to large CAPE (2000-4000+ J/kg) could still support a period of rapid storm intensification. This could include the evolution of supercell structure, posing a risk for severe hail and locally strong surface gusts. It is possible that isolated storm development may linger into the 01-03Z time frame. There may be a tendency for activity to develop north/northeastward into the Badlands of South Dakota, supported by forcing associated with strengthening warm advection along a remnant zone of stronger differential surface heating, before inhibition increases with the loss of daytime heating.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Supercell storms posing a risk for severe hail and a tornado or two appear increasingly likely across parts of north central Montana by 7-9 PM MDT.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Several discrete thunderstorms are in the process of developing across the higher terrain of central Montana, southwest through northwest of Lewistown. This may be supported by forcing for ascent associated with a corridor of low-level warm advection, and perhaps a subtle mid-level perturbation which is expected to migrate northeastward toward the Saskatchewan border through this evening. Beneath/within seasonably strong southwesterly mid/upper flow, including 50+ kt at 500 mb, deep-layer shear is more than sufficient for supercells, but boundary layer instability is initially modest to weak, which appears to be slowing/suppressing convective intensification. However, surface dew points have increased by 5 degrees F (into the lower 50s) or so the past few hours across the Lewistown area, with lower 60s dew points present to the northeast, across portions of Blaine, Phillip and perhaps northern Fergus county. As storms continue to develop northeastward into the better boundary layer moisture and instability by 01-03Z, considerable intensification appears possible, with storms posing increasing risk for severe hail. This may also coincide with enlargement of low-level hodographs which may provide support for the risk of a tornado or two. ..Kerr.. 06/29/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated supercell may transition to a small evolving mesoscale convective system while approaching the Glasgow vicinity through 10 PM CDT. Severe hail remains possible, with some potential for a tornado, before the risk for strong surface gusts becomes more prominent during the next few hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Strongest convection, including continuing supercell development, now generally appears north of the Missouri River, and appears likely to continue to propagate east-northeastward to the northwest of Fort Peck Lake, into the Glasgow vicinity by around 04Z. There gradually appears enough of a surface cold pool forming to support further upscale growth over the next few hours, aided by easterly inflow of increasingly moist and unstable air (CAPE of 1000-2000 J/kg), in the presence of strong deep-layer shear. As this occurs, severe weather potential seems likely to transition from a risk for large to occasionally very large hail, and some risk for a tornado, to mainly a risk for severe wind gusts across and northeast of Glasgow through 04-06z. ..Kerr.. 06/29/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: An organized cluster of thunderstorms may maintain strength and continue to pose a risk for hail and severe surface gusts, near and north of the Missouri River, across northeastern Montana into northwestern North Dakota through Midnight-2 AM MDT.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Large-scale mid/upper support for the ongoing convection may be in the process of decreasing, and activity is progressing into an environment with stronger inhibition associated with warmer elevated-mixed layer air. However, the small convective system appears to be maintaining strength across and east of the Glasgow area, likely aided by strong convergence along the cold pool, and perhaps weak low-level warm advection. This seems likely to persist at least into the 06-08Z time frame, as strong inflow continues to become characterized by increasing boundary layer moisture content and potential instability (CAPE in excess of 2000 J/kg) through the northeastern Montana/North Dakota border area. ..Kerr.. 06/29/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: While the primary wind threat has ended, additional cells capable of hail may develop tonight.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A potent bow echo has weakened as it moved into northwest ND and across the international border. An outflow boundary extends southwest from the original bow, with recent indications of new storms attempting to develop along it. Lift along the wind shift as well as continued warm/moist air advection above the cooling boundary layer may support a few severe storms capable of hail. These storms may remain elevated, thus a wind threat is not expected. If storm coverage becomes more than anticipated, additional areas may need to be added to the watch, in western or northern ND. Otherwise, the severe threat will continue to end from west to east behind the main outflow boundary. ..Jewell.. 06/29/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Storms have trended toward supercell mode over the last hour. Large hail, and perhaps a brief tornado are possible.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Storms that formed along the outflow boundary have gradually increased in intensity, with supercells now noted on radar. Once such storm over Richland County MT has broad rotation, with a very high echo top. Another supercell now exists over western McKenzie County ND, just northeast of the Richland cell. Both these cells are near the outflow boundary. Additional cells also continue to strengthen northeastward into Mountrail County. Given supercellular mode, low-level shear may more easily become incorporated into the updrafts despite moderate boundary layer CIN. Storms may also utilize enhanced vorticity as they interact with the outflow boundary, and a brief tornado cannot be ruled out. Large hail remains likely with steep lapse rates aloft and ample moisture (PWAT up to 1.50"). ..Jewell.. 06/29/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A complex of storms capable of damaging wind will continue east and southeast across North Dakota.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Severe storms that earlier produced hail over northwest ND have merged into an MCS, now moving eastward through the Minot area with measured severe winds at MIB. These storms are being fed by a southerly low-level jet, with ample moisture and instability upstream the inflow layer. Given current organization of these storms, they are likely to persist through the morning, traveling generally eastward. The most severe portion of this line is oriented north-south, and may encounter a more stable air mass directly to the east. However, the low-level jet orientation suggests southern parts of the line, now oriented in an east-west direction, may bow southeastward later this morning along the instability gradient.
